name: Water Curupira
iocPatterns: Multi-stage loader execution paths involving curl.exe and rundll32.exe
SOCKS proxy establishment on non-standard port 8008
Double file extensions (e.g., .docx.lnk) or embedded files (.img)
High frequency of requests to cloud repositories like Dropbox/Pastebin
keyCapabilities: Establishment of SOCKS proxies for internal tunneling
DNS tunneling and C2 communication over non-standard ports
recommendedActions: Block and alert on any attempts to modify FortiGate configurations or disable security features via CLI.
Monitor for the use of curl.exe combined with rundll32.exe in automated download/execution chains.
Implement EDR policies to block vssadmin shadow copy deletion commands.
Restrict access to non-standard ports (e.g., 8008, 1194, 2078) at the network perimeter.
Audit and restrict usage of nircmd on workstations and servers.
Implement detection for NTDS.dit extraction from Domain Controllers.
Scan and block known C2 IP addresses associated with Pikabot and Black Basta.
Block outbound traffic to high-risk cloud storage platforms like Pastebin or Dropbox from internal networks.
Audit incoming emails for 'thread-hijacking' indicators (suspicious replies on old email threads).
Segment OT/ICS networks to prevent malware progression from IT segments.
campaignsText: Water Curupira demonstrates a high operation tempo, shifting from broad-based spam campaigns using Qakbot to more targeted infrastructure disruption. The 2025 Poland Wiper attacks marks a significant escalation in their activities, where they moved beyond just stealing data to actively destroying hardware and firmware on RTUs and other energy utility components. Their transition to the Pikabot loader correlates with an increased sophistication in evading security tools, including the use of non-standard ports (8008, 13720) and automated extraction of domain controller credentials before deploying destructive wipers.
description: Water Curupira (TA577) is a sophisticated threat actor and affiliate of the Black Basta ransomware group that utilizes the Pikabot loader for multi-stage initial access. The group has demonstrated high technical proficiency by targeting critical infrastructure, utilizing advanced evasive techniques like FortiGate manipulation, and leveraging emerging technologies including LLM-generated scripts.
goals: Water Curupira's primary objectives involve high-value data exfiltration for ransom demands via the Black Basta ransomware ecosystem and, increasingly, the disruption of critical infrastructure. Their targeting profile is diverse but strategic, focusing on large organizations across South America and Europe, with a specific recent focus on energy providers and industrial sectors where technical outages can cause significant socioeconomic impact.
